reviews.reason: 3 critical issue(s) -- floor not tradeable (CDIO-00 sec.4)

reasons: A uses the stock layout: a tinted gradient hero, three identical numbered cards, centered section heads and a 'Most popular' badge

B's features section shows the product working: a transcript line with the commitment highlighted becomes a task, plus an integrations cell and a data-retention promise, laid out as a bento instead of interchangeable cards
B's hero visual pairs a quoted recording line with the task extracted from it, and the open-task count updates as boxes are checked, which makes the product concrete
B's pricing is the more realistic SaaS split (Team, then Business with SSO, audit log and retention), with the intro and billing toggle in a side column
B makes more deliberate choices: a single terracotta accent, dark mode, 44px touch targets, monospace metadata, one large and one compact testimonial, and motion that never hides content
A's features are an asymmetric bento with a real transcript-to-task demo (highlighted quote becomes an action item), not three numbered icon cards
B uses the stock template formula: gradient-tint hero, centered section headings, three equal feature cards, and a 'Most popular' badge
B has an em dash in the title and filler intro copy ('Three things, done well'); A's copy is plain and specific ('Our weekly ops call used to end with three people writing three different lists')
A's testimonials are laid out unevenly (one large, one compact with a rule between them); B's are two identical cards
A has a deliberate palette (slate with one terracotta accent), dark mode, and a mono type for metadata; B uses system fonts and a stock blue with a light-only theme
